# The Shadium

> The Shadium finds the shaded seats at sports venues. Pick a stadium and a game, and it shows which sections and seats will be in sun or shade at that game's real first-pitch time.

For MLB ballparks, The Shadium works out shade from the sun's position (NREL's Solar Position Algorithm), the shape of the stands, decks and roofs (measured from USGS lidar at 24 of the 30 parks), and the real first-pitch time from MLB's schedule. The MLB map shows a clear sky; the full finder for MiLB and NFL venues shows the forecast from Open-Meteo. See the full methodology, including accuracy and limitations, at https://theshadium.com/how-it-works.

## Coverage

- 182 venues across three leagues: 30 MLB ballparks, 120 Minor League Baseball (MiLB) parks, and 32 NFL stadiums.
- MLB ballpark pages show every section in sun or shade for any game, inning by inning, with the sections that get the most shade, a High, Medium or Low confidence label, and how high the sun gets each month.
- Nearly all MiLB and NFL pages are sun and shade guides: which side or sideline tends to shade first, plus seating, food and travel notes.

## URL patterns

- Venue guide: https://theshadium.com/stadium/{id} — e.g. /stadium/yankees, /stadium/dodgers, /stadium/durham-bulls
- League index: https://theshadium.com/league/{league} — /league/mlb, /league/milb, /league/nfl
- All stadiums index: https://theshadium.com/stadiums
- Methodology: https://theshadium.com/how-it-works
- Blog: https://theshadium.com/blog

## Notes

- The Shadium is an independent tool and is not affiliated with MLB, MiLB, the NFL, or any team.
- Shade predictions are strong guides, not guarantees; real bowls curve, rows vary, and weather changes.
